bullets.title: TSMC June Revenue +68% YoY; Q2 Record on AI Demand
bullets.body: TSMC reported June revenue of $13.8B, up 67.9% YoY and 6.2% MoM, driving record Q2 revenue of $39.63B (+36% YoY). Multiple fintwit accounts flagged this as a strong demand signal for contract chipmaking driven by AI. One note adds that revenue growth, while accelerating, has become more volatile on a month-to-month basis.

bullets.title: TSMC 1.4nm Process On Track; First Fab Nearing Completion
bullets.body: TSMC's 1.4nm process is reportedly seeing zero roadblocks, with the first fab nearing completion and pilot production expected as early as Q3 2027. This signals continued technology leadership runway beyond current 3nm/2nm ramp.

bullets.title: Citi Raises AAPL Price Target to $365 from $315, Maintains Buy
bullets.body: Citigroup raised its Apple price target to $365 from $315 while maintaining a Buy rating, one of the more notable PT lifts circulating on fintwit this morning.

bullets.title: Meta Announces $50B+ Data Center Expansion in Louisiana
bullets.body: Meta announced a data center investment exceeding $50B in Richland Parish, Louisiana, targeting 5GW of compute capacity and creating 1,000+ jobs. The scale underscores continued hyperscaler commitment to AI infrastructure buildout despite investor concerns about capex discipline.

bullets.title: Goldman Warns Chip Suppliers Face Multiple Compression if Hyperscaler Capex Pressured
bullets.body: Goldman flagged that hardware chip suppliers could face multiple compression even if earnings grow, should investor pressure on hyperscaler capex discipline intensify. The note highlights valuation risk as a distinct concern from fundamental earnings trajectory.

bullets.title: SK Hynix Record 15% Plunge Triggers KOSPI's 7th Circuit Breaker of 2026
bullets.body: SK Hynix fell a record 15% in a single session, dragging KOSPI down and triggering its 7th circuit breaker halt of 2026 (7 of 13 all-time halts have occurred this year). The selloff is being described as an 'AI winners unwind' with South Korean stocks now down 25.3% from their peak.

bullets.title: MS Remains Optimistic on Memory Cycle Duration Post-Nvidia NDR, Cautious on Peak Earnings
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flagged optimism on the duration of the memory cycle following a Nvidia non-deal roadshow, while cautioning that peak earnings power sustainability remains a concern. The distinction between cycle length vs. earnings peak is the key nuance.

bullets.title: AI Sovereignty Thesis Gaining Traction: Karp, Nadella, Benioff Converging
bullets.body: Satya Nadella's essay on the 'Reverse Information Paradox' — enterprises pay for AI with both money and proprietary data — is being seen as validation of Alex Karp's AI sovereignty thesis. One fintwit account notes Benioff (CRM) and Nadella (MSFT) are now echoing Karp (PLTR), suggesting a preference cascade toward data-independent AI platforms.

bullets.title: TSLA Valuation Called Excessive at 209x 2026 P/E; PEG 6x vs Mag 8 Avg 2x
bullets.body: One account flags TSLA trading at 209x 2026 P/E despite ~35% long-term EPS growth, implying a PEG of 6x versus the Magnificent 8 average of 2x. The author frames it as difficult to support the valuation even as a bull on the company.

bullets.title: Intel Unveils Starfire Space-Grade SoCs on 18A Process
bullets.body: Intel unveiled its Starfire SoCs featuring space-grade survivability built on its 18A process node, a product development milestone for its foundry and advanced chip roadmap.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz Closure Threat + Explosions Near Bandar Abbas Escalate Energy Risk
bullets.body: Iran state TV warned the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US ends interference, while explosions were reported near Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island. Bahrain confirmed its air defenses intercepted multiple Iranian aerial attacks. Brent crude rose 2.9% to ~$78/bbl on the tensions, with NDX off 1.0% and 10yr yields up 8bp to 4.57%.

bullets.title: US Futures Under Pressure: SPX -0.3%, NDX -1.0% on Iran Tensions and Asia Weakness
bullets.body: Pre-market summary: SPX fell 0.3%, NDX fell 1.0%, Brent crude +2.9% to $78/bbl, 10yr treasury yields +8bp to 4.57%, Bitcoin -1.6% to $63.1K, Gold -1.1% to $4,104/oz. Korean market selloff and Strait of Hormuz closure driving the risk-off tone.

bullets.title: US Power Costs Surge to 17-Year Highs on Data Center Demand
bullets.body: Natural gas power costs hit $90/MWh in 2026, the highest in at least 17 years, while solar and onshore wind costs jumped more than 10%. Accelerating data-center demand is cited as the primary driver, a structural cost headwind for hyperscalers and AI infrastructure operators.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Bottleneck Shifts from Chips to Physical Build-Out
bullets.body: A WhiteFiber Q1 call detail circulating on fintwit: enterprise customers already hold 2027 GPU orders but lack deployment-ready infrastructure, suggesting the compute supply bottleneck has migrated from chip availability to data center construction and placement capacity.

bullets.title: US Equity Positioning Back to 6-Month Bullish Extremes — Contrarian Risk
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough flags that US equity consensus bullishness has returned to 6-month highs, a potential contrarian signal heading into a heavy data and earnings week.

bullets.title: Citi Downgrades UK Equities to Underweight from Overweight
bullets.body: Citigroup cut its UK stock market rating to Underweight, citing the market's defensive and commodity-heavy composition as less appealing in the current earnings growth environment, despite attractive absolute valuations.

bullets.title: Netflix Exploring Always-On TV Channels by Genre
bullets.body: Netflix is reportedly considering launching always-on TV channels that play genre-specific content (shows, movies) continuously, per NYMag. The move would represent a format shift toward traditional linear-style viewing within the streaming platform.

bullets.title: SMCI Gets Citigroup PT Raise to $33 from $31
bullets.body: Citigroup raised its Super Micro Computer price target to $33 from $31, a modest but directionally positive revision circulating on fintwit this morning.

bullets.title: Ukraine Hits All 10 Major Russian Oil Refineries; 25%+ of Refining Capacity Offline
bullets.body: Ukraine has now successfully struck all 10 of Russia's largest oil refineries in 2026, with analyst estimates suggesting more than 25% of Russian refining capacity has been knocked offline — a geopolitical supply factor contributing to the oil price rally.

bullets.title: Asian Market Rout: Shanghai -2.1% to 3-Month Lows, Nikkei -1.9% Overnight
bullets.body: Broad Asian weakness overnight: Shanghai composite dropped 2.1% to new 3-month lows, and the Nikkei fell 1.9%. Combined with the KOSPI circuit breaker halt, the risk-off tone in Asia is feeding into US futures pressure.
